notes:
I couldn't write these notes because my research tools stopped working before I read a single page.

I tried to open nine sources at once: Enduring Word on Isaiah 20, the Bible Hub commentary pages for verses 1–6, Gill on StudyLight and the NET Bible notes. The system rejected the request with a "tool use limit exceeded" error. When I tried one search instead, it told me I had no tool calls left for this turn.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. I didn't read any of them, so any notes I wrote now would come from my own memory with no sources behind them. That would break your rules, so I've left the notes out entirely.

If you ask me again in a new message, my tools should be available again, and I'll do the research in this order:
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word; Bible Hub (Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Gill and others for each verse); StudyLight; Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon and Grace to You (gty.org), Ligonier and The Gospel Coalition, and the LCMS and 1517 sites. I'd only include a verse here if their own teachers really disagree.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship; New Advent (which has the Church Fathers) and catholic.com for Catholic readings, and oca.org for Orthodox ones. I'd cover popular modern teaching only if these sites discuss it in connection with Isaiah 20.

The notes would follow your format, "v. 1: …" through "v. 6: …", with a URL after each point. Anything I can't find would be left out.
